course_name_original: Cálculo y Diseño de Máquinas II (29104219)

learning_outcomes.text: Students must have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
Students must have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.

The student must know the different existing techniques for the correct design of machines and their elements, depending on their working conditions and expected life, as well as the techniques for product calculation and verification and related tests, following the different existing regulations and specifications in each case.
Have an integral vision of the functioning of machines in a mechanical assembly.
Address the design and selection of typical machine elements.
Select materials, processes, and treatments for specific applications.
Present solutions for different machine problems that may arise.
Compare different solutions for the same problem.

assessment_methods.method: Written test evaluating reports, assignments, projects, and classroom participation

assessment_rules: The evaluation is based on a final exam with two parts: a written test (20%) and a theory and problems test (80%). To pass the course, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be obtained. The same tests and percentages apply for the extraordinary examination. A single final evaluation is available for eligible students, covering all course content and competencies.
